subject: Business Models
title: Time-Limited Trials vs Free Tiers
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Time-Limited Trials vs Free Tiers.

hook.text: Netflix offers a free trial for 30 days. Slack offers a free tier forever. Very different strategies.

buildup.text: Trials give full access temporarily. Free tiers give limited access permanently. Each has trade-offs.

discovery.text: Trials create urgency: use it or lose it. Free tiers create habit: use it long enough to need more.

twist.text: Netflix killed its free trial in 2020. It found trials attracted deal-seekers, not loyal long-term subscribers.

climax.text: The choice depends on your product. High-switching-cost products benefit from trials. Network tools need free tiers.

punchline.text: 30 days free or forever limited. The right model depends on how habits form.

quiz.question: Why did Netflix eliminate its free trial?
options: Trials attracted deal-seekers rather than long-term subscribers

details.summary: Time-limited trials give full access for a set period then require payment, while free tiers provide permanent limited access with optional upgrades. Trials create urgency and higher conversion rates but smaller user bases, while free tiers maximize reach but have lower conversion rates.
details.whyItMatters: Choosing between trials and free tiers is a foundational business model decision. Trials work better for products with high per-user costs and clear value propositions..
takeaways: Trials create urgency but end the relationship if users do not pay
Free tiers maintain the user relationship indefinitely for future conversion
The choice depends on marginal costs, network effects, and product complexity

faq.question: When should a product use a time-limited trial instead of a free tier?
faq.answer: When per-user costs are high and supporting free users is expensive. When the product's value is best demonstrated through full access. When the target audience is enterprise buyers with budget. When the product does not benefit from network effects that require a large free user base.

faq.question: Can businesses combine trials with free tiers effectively?
faq.answer: Yes, reverse trials start users on premium then downgrade to free, combining both approaches. Some products offer a permanent free tier plus additional trial periods for premium features. The hybrid approach maximizes both immediate conversion and long-term conversion opportunities.
